rows.en:
Nice to meet you all.
I'm Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
...So we've finally come to the last story.
And yet the seventh person still hasn't shown up.
That means I'll be the one telling the last story.
It's {a}{f:|}, isn't it?{p}What do you say?
Would it be a problem for you if you can't hear seven scary stories?
It would be a problem
I'll fudge the article somehow

I see.
I'm relieved to hear that.
...Well, you see, the truth is there's a story that if you hear seven scary stories about this school, something bad will happen.
So I thought it would be better if this ended safely, with just the six of us finishing our stories.
I'm truly glad.
It looks like this will end safely after all...{p}

Well then, let me begin my story.
This is a story I'd decided not to tell if seven people had gathered.
So if my turn had come around any earlier, I would never have told it.
That's how dangerous a story it is.
After all, there's no telling where it might be watching from.
What's 'it,' you ask?
A doll.
Do you find that funny?
{a}{f:|}, do you think I've lost my mind?
Well, I don't mind if you do.
If you mock that doll, you're the one who'll be cursed, that's all.
...But I suppose it's all right now.
It doesn't look like seven people will gather anymore, so it seems safe to tell it.
So, let me tell you.
The story of the doll that lives in this school.{p}

...Do you all like dolls?
There are all kinds of dolls.
Japanese dolls, French dolls... ones that capture the character of their country.
Straw effigies, and cursing dolls like the ones used in black magic.
Even the stuffed animals everyone loves are dolls.
Ventriloquist dummies and marionettes... dolls that call for special skill.
We sum them all up in one word, 'doll,' but their uses and looks vary widely.
But you know, there's just one thing they all have in common.
Just one point that every doll shares.
...And that is that they have souls.
Rather than saying they 'have' souls, perhaps it's better to say a soul enters them.
A doll, you see, is just what the word says: a thing made in human form, isn't it?
Sensing the feelings of the one who made it or the one who owns it, a doll begins to take on a soul.{p}{a}{f:|}, what image do you have of dolls?
Cute
Scary
Warm
Nostalgic

I see.
There are quite a lot of people like that, you know.
There are plenty of ghost stories about dolls, after all.
Dolls whose hair grows, dolls that shed tears.
I find dolls frightening, too.
Often, when there's a doll sitting all alone in a room, looking lonely, my eyes can't help drifting toward it.
For some reason, I feel as if the doll is watching me...
...I'm sorry.
I was telling you about the doll that lives in the school.{p}
To tell the truth, I don't know how long that doll has been at this school.{p}

But there's no doubt that it's here.
And it appears before you know it.
{a}{f:|}, don't you see what I'm trying to tell you?
Are you wondering what on earth this doll is?
Yes, I'd think it only natural to wonder.
You may be bewildered by this story at first too, {a}{f:|}.
But it's all right.
By the time my story is over, I think you'll believe in the doll that lives in this school too.
There are a number of stories about this doll.
That's how well known it is.
What kind of doll is it, you ask?{p}

...Let's see.
If I had to put it into words, I'd say it's very close to a human... that it resembles a human.
It's life-size, too.
Perhaps just slightly smaller than a person.
Yes, if you picture it as about the size of a big child, that should do.
Its skin is pure white, its hair is black, and its large eyes are its most striking feature.
It's a beautiful doll, but seen another way, you could say it's eerie because it looks too much like a human.
Every joint is made to move, and I hear it's crafted with real precision.
Only its mouth doesn't open.
Probably because it was made to look as human as possible.
If the mouth opens, it inevitably ends up looking like a ventriloquist's dummy.
Its features are... well, they seem like a woman's.
But some people say it looks like a beautiful boy, so perhaps the best way to put it is an androgynous beauty, neither male nor female.
And of course, no one knows who made the doll, either.
Besides, I don't really know much about it myself.
I haven't actually seen it; I've only pieced together what I've heard from various people.
So there are a few places where the stories don't agree.
Some say its eyes were frighteningly large, or that its ears were pointed, or that its mouth gaped wide open...
Why do the accounts differ so much, you ask?
Well, it can't be helped.
No one who has seen that doll is left now.
Because they die, you see.
Every last person who sees that doll.{p}

But the doll is here.
In this school, without a doubt.
Do you know how I can say that?
You're still a first-year, {a}{f:|}.
You may not know.
But those of us in second year and above know.
And we're always trembling with fear.
Wondering when our turn will come.{p}

...This school, you see, offers one sacrifice to the doll every year.
Rather than 'offers,' it would be more accurate to say someone ends up becoming the sacrifice.
In fact, I don't even know if it's only one.
One is just the minimum; in truth, any number of students may have fallen victim.
You've been listening to scary stories just now, haven't you, {a}{f:|}?
And I think you'll go on hearing stories of that kind from now on, too.
But you know, there's a rumor that at least some of the people in those stories were killed by that doll.
However they die, a single doll is always lurking in the shadows behind it.
They say the people chosen as sacrifices are always terrified by the sight of the doll.
...Oh, yes. It's right around this time of year that the doll's sacrifices die.
And I haven't heard of anyone becoming a sacrifice yet this year...
So this year's victim may turn up any time now.
What I'll tell you, then, is the story of the victim who became the doll's sacrifice last year.{p}

Last year's victim came from my class.
He was a classmate of mine, a student named Shoichi Kanai.
He was always jumpy, with eyes that seemed afraid of something.
I suppose that was just his personality.
If you called out to him from behind, he'd always jump.
And whenever there was a noise somewhere, he'd look around nervously until he found out what caused it.
At first, even those of us with him would be startled, wondering what had happened, but once we understood it was his nature, his habit, we got completely used to it.
That's exactly why we didn't realize it.
That he was afraid of the doll.{p}

As I remember it, the first time he started talking about the doll was when we were passing by the incinerator.
Four or five of us were idly walking around there after school.
It was when we passed in front of the incinerator.
Suddenly, Kanai stopped in his tracks.{p}

And with that usual frightened look in his eyes, he was staring fixedly at the incinerator.
I was the first to notice.
By then I was used to his habits, so I didn't think much of it.
"What's wrong?
Did you see something again?"
I spoke to him, trying my best not to startle him.
Then, in a trembling voice, he said,
"...There's a doll.
Inside the incinerator, a doll is calling me."{p}

Blurting that out, he staggered toward the incinerator.
I was startled.
After all, the incinerator was burning garbage right then, and bright red flames were roaring up out of it.
"What are you doing, Kanai?
That's dangerous!"
The others joined in to stop him.{p}
Maybe our stopping him did the trick, because after a while he suddenly came back to himself and walked briskly off as if nothing had happened.{p}

After that, he began to see the doll at every turn.
What do you think, {a}{f:|}?{p}Do you think what Kanai saw was an illusion?
Or do you think the doll really existed?
I think it was an illusion
I think the doll really existed
I can't say yet

...I see.
I think that's a wise judgment.
Even as we sit here now, there's no saying the doll isn't creeping up on us.
...No, perhaps one of us has already seen that doll.{p}

This is a digression, but apparently people really do see hallucinations quite often.
Ghosts and the like, for example. They say most of those are hallucinations.
Of course, real spirits exist too, but in most cases they're hallucinations, apparently.
When you're tired, or when your mind is unstable, you end up seeing things like that.
And cases of seeing a doll at such times are especially common, I hear.
Actually, I've seen one myself...
No, not that doll.
After all, it happened before I entered this high school.
There was a Japanese doll lying in a room where no one should have been.
A long-haired doll of a little child.
The instant after I blinked, though, it was gone.
Well, that doesn't matter.{p}
...So, back to Kanai.{p}
The second time Kanai saw that doll was two days later.

We were playing softball in gym class when Kanai suddenly went berserk.
He ran all over the field, swinging a bat around.
"Stay away!
Don't come near me!"
Everyone there froze.
After all, it was those of us watching who were in danger.
He swung that bat with eyes that seemed to see something that wasn't there.
That was when I heard some people whispering about it.
That's how I came to learn the story of this school's doll, too.
The gym teacher hesitated for a moment before stopping him.
I still remember the pitying look on the teacher's face then.

...But don't you find it strange?
Our school has a cursed doll like that, so why doesn't everyone just quit?
Students who enroll without knowing can't help it, but the teachers, and the students who've seen the reality for themselves... why don't they quit, I wonder?{p}Don't you find it strange?
I find it strange
Not really

Exactly.
I found it strange too.
So I asked around among the people who knew the doll story.
And I learned one fact.
First, the teachers apparently never come to harm.
So it doesn't concern them.
And the student is apparently chosen before they even enter the school.
It's only a rumor, mind you.
But they say the principal knows.
Among those who pass this school's entrance exam, for some reason, there's always at least one who actually failed.
And that one, they say, is the sacrifice the doll has chosen.
That's why every year a few students slip into this school who never should have been accepted.
And the principal knows it.
Knows it, and lets them in.
The students who are meant to become sacrifices.
Don't you think that's a frightening story?{p}

But you know, in exchange for receiving its sacrifice, the doll supposedly leads this school to victory in every kind of tournament and gets plenty of students into top universities on their first try.
...It's nothing more than a rumor, of course.
So perhaps one of us here is one of them.
{a}{f:|}, it might even be you.{p}
...And that's the end of my story.{p}It seems the seventh person isn't coming after all, so this gathering has come to a safe end.
Then let's go home
Wait a moment. Please tell me more about Kanai.

What's the matter?
Has the doll story caught your interest, {a}{f:|}?
Or is it Kanai you're interested in?
...Well, all right.
I meant to wrap things up early, you know.
But if you want to hear it that badly, I'll go on.
With the story of Kanai's tragedy.{p}

After that incident on the field, the talk was all over school: Kanai was that year's victim.
And it's true that from then on, more and more people looked at him with pity.
After that, Kanai's strange behavior began to stand out.
In the middle of a test, he'd suddenly start tearing up his answer sheet, then clutch his head and scream...
"Leave me alone!
I don't want to go!
So stop trying to lure me!"
And then he'd slump over his desk and pass out...{p}

Even seeing that, the teacher kept up a calm front, as if nothing had been seen.
"...Looks like Kanai isn't feeling well.
Someone take him to the nurse's office."
That one remark was the end of it.
Even though the teacher knew perfectly well it was the doll's doing.
Teachers are awful, aren't they?
The principal must have sworn them to silence, or they're getting something out of it.{p}

Anyone could see that Kanai was wasting away.
He'd never had much of a build to begin with, but in less than a week after he saw the doll at the incinerator, he'd grown as thin as a skeleton.
And day by day, people stopped going near Kanai.
But that couldn't be helped.
If you were just near him, he'd try to strangle you or start thrashing around.
It looked as if the people around him would be killed before Kanai ever became the doll's sacrifice.
That's how dangerous Kanai had become.
The teacher told him to stay home from school, too.
But it seemed less out of concern than because the teacher didn't want to be involved.{p}

But Kanai wouldn't stay home.
As if coming to school were his duty, he came no matter what.
Just sitting through class seemed painful for him.
All he was doing was sitting in his chair, yet he looked worn out and did nothing but sigh.
The teacher didn't say anything anymore.
It was maybe a week later.
All the classes were over, and as I was about to go home...{p}

Kanai was standing beside my desk.
As if he wanted to say something, and looking miserable.
To be honest, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't scared.
I tried hard to act normal, but it shows in your manner, doesn't it?
Without meaning to, I seem to have avoided meeting his eyes.
"You're scared of me, aren't you?
Nobody will listen to me.
...Please. Will you let me talk something over with you?"
I'm sure that's what a ghost's voice sounds like.
A voice so faint you could barely make it out, and yet it echoed strangely in my head.
And a dark, gloomy force that made it impossible to refuse once he asked.
I found myself nodding, just as he wanted.
The pitying looks everyone gave Kanai had spread to me too.
"...Let's talk on the way home."
If I could, I'd have rather talked in the classroom.
There were still people there.
I thought they'd help me if anything happened.
But I did as he said.
For some reason, the mood left me no choice but to agree.{p}{a}{f:|}.
Do you think I'm a pathetic sort of man for that?
I think you're pathetic
I don't think so at all

The hallway was dead silent.
Usually at that hour it was packed with students heading home, but for some reason there wasn't a soul in sight that day; it was utterly silent.
I started walking side by side with Kanai.
Down the empty hallway...

"...I'm going to die today."
It came out of nowhere.
Who knows what was on his mind, but Kanai murmured those words.
I didn't know what to say.
When I didn't answer, Kanai started talking on his own.
"...You know, for the past two or three days, I've been seeing the doll the whole time.
I know now, too. Every year this school has to hand over one sacrifice to the doll, right?"
And then he looked at me.{p}

My body was trembling.
I couldn't look Kanai in the face.
For some reason, I felt guilty.
I couldn't shake the feeling that Kanai was blaming me.
I couldn't shake the feeling that he resented me for knowing the doll story and not telling him.
I'm not responsible.
It's not my fault, either.
Besides, I only learned the doll story after it became clear he was the sacrifice.
Even so, my legs went rigid, and as I walked they felt as if they weren't my own.{p}

I could hardly breathe; I felt like I was going to die.
I kept my mouth shut, and it was all I could do to mechanically put one foot in front of the other.
"...The doll calls me.
I don't know why the doll calls me.
Or why I was the one chosen...
But it's a fact that I'm being called.
And soon I'm going to die.
The doll won't leave me.
Look, it's right beside you now.
Right now you're walking between the doll and me."
With that, Kanai suddenly thrust his face right in front of mine as I looked away.{p}

His face was smiling.
Is that what a skull looks like when it smiles?
It was a terribly sad smile.
And I ended up meeting Kanai's gaze.
"...Look, the doll just put its hand on your shoulder.
What's wrong?
Can't you see it, Arai?
...Looks like the doll has taken a liking to you."
I wanted to run, but my legs wouldn't obey me.
As if I'd been hypnotized, my feet just kept moving forward.
My fear reached its peak.
If I had opened my mouth, my heart would have leapt right out of it.
Kanai laughed: hee hee hee...
When he laughed, his breath puffed across my face.
And how cold that breath was...{p}

"...The doll won't leave my side.
It even follows me home.
When I'm asleep, it stands by my pillow the whole time.
Just staring at me.
Is it real...?
Or is it a dream...?
I can't take it anymore.
When I get in the bath, the doll is in the tub with half its face sticking out of the water.
It won't leave my side for even a second.
Just when I thought I'd be better off dead, the doll gave me a wide grin.
And a voice echoed in my head.
'You die tomorrow...'
That was yesterday.
So, you see, today I'm going to die.
Which brings me to what I wanted to ask you..."{p}

He laughed again.
I couldn't look away anymore.
His face was so close to mine that our skin almost touched.{p}...What will you do?
Do you want to hear what Kanai wanted to ask me?
I want to hear it
I don't want to hear it

"...The truth is.
These sacrifices end next year.
Whoever becomes the sacrifice next year will be the last one.
That's what the doll says.
...Isn't that right?"{p}

With that, he abruptly pulled his face away from me and turned his eyes to my left shoulder.
I deliberately looked away from that direction.
My left shoulder, where nothing should have been, felt heavy.
Was the doll resting its face there?
Then Kanai brought his face close to mine again.{p}

"...It says so.
So I want you to make sure.
Whether that one is definitely at this school.
If they're here, there's no problem.
Then this school will finally be freed from its many curses.
I think the strange incidents that have happened at this school will stop, too.
The name is......"{p}

I heard it.
That person's name.
If that person becomes the doll's victim this year, it will all be over.
That person was at this school, all right.
So soon, it's going to happen.
The final sacrificial rite.
That person is, well......... right here among us.
Among the people gathered here now.
I can't say any more than that.
All Kanai asked of me was to find that person, after all.
Kanai died right after that.
It was a heart attack.{p}

He stretched out both hands as if to grab at something near my left shoulder, and died just like that, his mouth flapping open and shut.
But clutched in his hands were several strands of black hair.
Not my hair.
Kanai never once touched my hair, you see.
Was it the hair of the doll that no one could see...?
I don't know.
He may have been holding it from the start.{p}

...Now my story really is over.
I pray that none of you ever sees that doll.
Though unless someone becomes the victim, the sacrifices won't end.
...In the end, the seventh person never showed up.
Which means this meeting is over.
Well then, I'll be heading home first. Excuse me.
...With that, Arai got up from his seat as if fleeing.{p}

"Ah...!"
When {f:I|I} tried to stop Arai, he slipped right through my grasp and hurried out of the club room.{p}

...What a nasty story Arai had told us.
{f:I|I} looked around at the people who remained.
Everyone had their faces down.
They looked frightened, and angry, too.{p}
